notes.title: GOOG & AMZN — inflated trailing EPS
notes.text: Q2 2026 included one-time investment gains (Alphabet ~$99B, Amazon ~$53B pre-tax, largely Anthropic stakes), so trailing P/E is flattered — for the stocks and for the Magnificent 7 median. Alphabet's Q3 2026 partly reversed this with an $8.7B loss on equity securities (−$0.55/share). Forward P/E is the cleaner read.

notes.title: META — depressed trailing EPS
notes.text: Q3 2025 carried a one-time tax charge (EPS $1.05), so trailing P/E overstates the multiple.

notes.title: XOM — depressed trailing EPS
notes.text: Q1 2026 absorbed ~$0.92/share of negative timing effects and Q2 2026 ~$0.63/share of impairments and reserve additions, so trailing P/E overstates the multiple. Consensus expects 2027 earnings below 2026 as the oil-price spike fades.

notes.title: NKE — flattered trailing EPS
notes.text: Q4 FY2026 (May 2026) included a one-time +$0.52/share benefit from expected tariff refunds, so trailing P/E looks far cheaper than forward.

notes.title: UBER — trailing EPS mostly one-offs
notes.text: Q3 2025 included a ~$2.30/share tax valuation-allowance release, and every quarter swings with revaluations of equity stakes (±$1.5B pre-tax). Forward P/E is the cleaner read. Growth uses Simply Wall St, since Zacks computes off the tax-inflated 2025 base.
